subject: small corner when two segment cross at their origin

messages.author: 7198113a7c71c5f8
messages.subject: small corner when two segment cross at their origin
parts:
Dear ggplotters,

geom_segment accepts the parameter size, which can be used to control the thickness of a segment.
I was wondering if it would be possible to have some sort of justification (i.e. not centered) for the size.
Something like text justification, where the side of the segment which grows can be selected.

Specifically, I would like to avoid the small corner that appears when two segments cross at their origin.

df <- data.frame(x=c(1,1), xend=c(2,1), y=c(1,1), yend=c(1,2))
ggplot(df) + geom_segment(aes(x=x, xend=xend, y=y, yend=yend), size=5)

Best,
Didac

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: small corner when two segment cross at their origin
parts:
Does adding lineend="square" address the goal?  This works regardless of the way the lines are rotated, so you don't need to calculate the justification based on the angle of the lines.

ggplot(df) + geom_segment(aes(x=x, xend=xend, y=y, yend=yend), size=5, lineend="square")

-Will
